## Summary

Files a DES-072 correction (`kind=factual`, `round=1`) against the closed cluster-3 mission, recording two things the audit trail did not show.

**The truncation.** The round-1 evidence entry was written as:

```yaml
- name: PR #515 merged as 6f61406 — 6/6 CI checks green, 17 review threads resolved
```

YAML discarded everything from `#515` onward as a comment, leaving `name: PR` while `status: pass` survived intact. The evidence was real; its description was destroyed by the parser and ethos accepted it silently. That underlying defect is fixed in PR #517 (`244b6c3`), which now refuses truncated values across all four submitted-artifact schemas.

**The out-of-band repair, which is why this correction exists.** I fixed that entry on 2026-09-11 by hand-editing `results.yaml` (`865c015`, merged `c846910`). That was the wrong remedy. `ethos-11fy`'s interim guidance names hand-editing `results.yaml` explicitly as a thing not to do, and `ethos mission correct` already existed as the sanctioned additive-only path. A clean file with no account of how it got clean is worse for an audit trail than a visibly corrected one.

## Why now

The operator asked why a closed-mission amend mechanism was still an open P1 when one had been built. It had — DES-072, SETTLED — and `ethos-11fy` was stale, filed 2026-08-07 and never closed out when the feature landed. Closing it on inspection alone would have repeated the defect this repo keeps finding, so the feature was dogfooded by filing this real correction first.

`ethos-11fy` is now closed, with all three of its stated requirements verified in code rather than asserted:

- additive-only correction event on the mission event log — `internal/mission/correct.go:50`
- scoped to closed missions specifically, the inverse of every other write path's open-only gate — `correct.go:209`
- never mutates or hides the original record — verified: `results.yaml` unchanged, only a new log file added

## Verification

```
$ ethos mission correct m-2026-09-10-001 --file .tmp/correct-...yaml
corrected: m-2026-09-10-001 kind=factual round=1 by claude

$ ethos mission log m-2026-09-10-001
  - 2026-09-10 11:08 PDT  create   by claude  worker=bwk evaluator=rsc
  - 2026-09-10 14:17 PDT  result   by bwk  round=1 verdict=pass
  - 2026-09-10 14:17 PDT  close    by claude  status=closed verdict=pass round=1
  - 2026-09-13 08:59 PDT  correct  by claude  kind=factual round=1

$ git status --short .punt-labs/ethos/
A  .../m-2026-09-10-001/log-...jsonl        # additive only; results.yaml untouched
```

docs-only — Phase 3 verification N/A. No runnable code touched; the diff is a single sealed mission-log entry.

tool_input.name: bwk-pii
tool_input.prompt:
One small fix on branch `chore/mission-correction-audit` in <repo> (PR #518). Do NOT push — commit and report; the leader pushes.

## The finding (Copilot + qodo independently; I verified it before delegating)

`internal/hook/audit_content.go` — `promptBearingKeys` names the `tool_input` keys the PII sweep runs over. It lists: body, content, description, instructions, message, notes, prompt, query, reason, subject, summary, text.

**`command` is not in that set.** So a Bash tool call's `command` string is never swept, and an address-shaped run inside it is sealed verbatim into a git-tracked audit chunk — in both `tool_input.command` and `tool_input_preview`. Confirmed on this branch: a `bd update` command carrying `[redacted-email]` sits unredacted in the sealed chunk at `.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/2026-09-07-.../audit-1789088839254251053-1789315221719063093.jsonl` lines 70 and 72.

The inconsistency is the defect: `send_email`'s inputs *are* redacted by this policy, so the system states a protection for address-shaped content and then misses it on the one tool that carries the most model-authored free text in the whole system.

The code's own doc comment already prescribes the fix: *"Add a key here when a tool starts carrying model-authored text under a new name. Widening the set can only redact more; it cannot leak."*

## What to do

Add `command` to `promptBearingKeys`. Verify the doc comment's claim holds for this key rather than assuming — specifically confirm that widening to `command` cannot break a legitimate non-prose value. Check every tool in this repo that takes a `command` key, not just Bash.

Then look at the same question one step wider, because this is a class not an instance: are there other `tool_input` keys in active use carrying model-authored free text that are absent from the set? Enumerate the tool surface and report what you checked and what you found, including "nothing else" if that is the answer. Do not add keys speculatively — a key earns its place by a tool actually writing prose under it, which is how `query` earned its place per the existing comment.

## Tests

A regression test proving a Bash `command` containing an address is redacted to `[redacted-email]`, covering both `tool_input.command` and `tool_input_preview`. Confirm it FAILS against pre-fix code and paste that output — a redaction test that has never been observed failing proves nothing.

Also pin the negative: a `command` with no address must be byte-identical after the sweep, so this does not start rewriting ordinary shell lines.

## Scope

Just this. Do NOT attempt to redact or regenerate the already-sealed chunks on this branch — they are sealed, hand-editing one breaks its seal, and `ethos audit quarantine` is the documented path if that were ever needed. This fix is forward-looking: future chunks are clean. Say so plainly in the CHANGELOG entry rather than implying existing chunks are scrubbed.

For context on why the existing chunk is not being scrubbed: that address is already present in 11 tracked files on main, including `.punt-labs/ethos/identities/jfreeman.yaml` where it belongs by design, and the operator has previously ruled that this class of exposure does not matter because it is already public. The forward-looking policy consistency is the part worth fixing.

## Gates

`make check` green with race. Report BOTH the `ok` count and the `FAIL` count — a zero FAIL alone cannot distinguish nothing-failed from nothing-ran. Pipe through `tee`, never redirect. No suppressions. CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]`.

## Summary

Two things, both about the audit trail's integrity.

### 1. A DES-072 correction against m-2026-09-10-001

Files a correction (`kind=factual`, `round=1`) against the closed cluster-3 mission, recording two facts the audit trail did not show.

**The truncation.** The round-1 evidence entry was written as:

```yaml
- name: PR #515 merged as 6f61406 — 6/6 CI checks green, 17 review threads resolved
```

YAML discarded everything from `#515` onward as a comment, leaving `name: PR` while `status: pass` survived intact. The evidence was real; its description was destroyed by the parser and ethos accepted it silently. That underlying defect is fixed in PR #517 (`244b6c3`).

**The out-of-band repair, which is why this correction exists.** I fixed that entry on 2026-09-11 by hand-editing `results.yaml` (`865c015`, merged `c846910`). That was the wrong remedy. `ethos-11fy`'s interim guidance names hand-editing `results.yaml` explicitly as a thing not to do, and `ethos mission correct` already existed as the sanctioned additive-only path. A clean file with no account of how it got clean is worse for an audit trail than a visibly corrected one.

### 2. `command` added to the audit PII sweep

Found by Copilot and qodo independently on this PR, and verified: `promptBearingKeys` in `internal/hook/audit_content.go` did not include `command`, so a Bash tool call's command string was never swept and an address inside it sealed verbatim into a git-tracked chunk — in both `tool_input.command` and `tool_input_preview`.

The defect is the inconsistency: `send_email` inputs *are* redacted by this policy, so the system states a protection for address-shaped content and then misses it on the tool carrying the most model-authored free text. The code's own doc comment prescribes the remedy — *"Add a key here when a tool starts carrying model-authored text under a new name. Widening the set can only redact more; it cannot leak."*

**This is forward-looking only.** The already-sealed chunks on this branch are not scrubbed: hand-editing a sealed chunk breaks its seal, and `ethos audit quarantine` is the documented path if that were ever warranted. It is not warranted here — that address is already present in 11 tracked files on `main`, including `.punt-labs/ethos/identities/jfreeman.yaml` where it belongs by design, so this is not a novel exposure. The policy consistency is the part worth fixing.

## Correction to this PR's own description

The first version of this description said "the diff is a single sealed mission-log entry." That was wrong. The commit contains **three** files — the correction log plus two session audit chunks swept in by `git add -A`. Per DES-058 sealed chunks travel in the same commit as the work, so their presence is correct; the description was not. Fixed here rather than left standing, since a PR description that misstates its own diff is the same defect this branch is about.

## Verification

```
$ ethos mission correct m-2026-09-10-001 --file ...
corrected: m-2026-09-10-001 kind=factual round=1 by claude

$ ethos mission log m-2026-09-10-001
  - 2026-09-10 11:08 PDT  create   by claude  worker=bwk evaluator=rsc
  - 2026-09-10 14:17 PDT  result   by bwk  round=1 verdict=pass
  - 2026-09-10 14:17 PDT  close    by claude  status=closed verdict=pass round=1
  - 2026-09-13 08:59 PDT  correct  by claude  kind=factual round=1

$ git status --short .punt-labs/ethos/
A  .../m-2026-09-10-001/log-...jsonl        # additive only; results.yaml untouched
```

`ethos-11fy` (the sole open P1, "closed missions have no correction mechanism") was closed on the back of this — it was stale, filed 2026-08-07 and never closed when DES-072 shipped. All three of its stated requirements verified in code rather than asserted: additive-only event (`correct.go:50`), closed-missions-only gate (`correct.go:209`), original never mutated (verified — `results.yaml` unchanged).
